The shipped plugin carried the tests' tooling, not the tests

PR playground for #4030: dropping test and build configs from plugins/ork/hooks.

The build already excluded the tests themselves (__tests__, *.d.ts, *.map), so the shipped plugin had no test to run. It kept the seven config files those tests are run with: four vitest manifests, two tsconfigs, and the esbuild bundler script. Seven files shipped to every install, read by nothing, and referencing devDependencies the mirror stopped declaring when #3971 stripped them.

Flip the consumer, watch what reads a config

Pick what executes against an installed plugin. Only the developer running the source tree's suite reads any of the seven; Claude Code — the only thing that runs the shipped tree — reads none of them.

filewhat it configuresread by the selected consumer?
vitest.config.tsunit suite: projects, coverage thresholds, setup file
vitest.bench.config.tsbenchmark suite (the vitest 5 migration's fixture config)
vitest.property.config.tsfast-check property suite
vitest.setup.tsper-test setup loaded by the unit config
tsconfig.jsonsource compile graph (bundles are prebuilt by esbuild)
tsconfig.test.jsontype coverage of the tests the plugin does not ship
esbuild.config.mjsbuilds dist/ bundles — already built before the mirror runs

The fix: seven excludes, same list, same block

--exclude='vitest.config.ts'         --exclude='vitest.bench.config.ts'
--exclude='vitest.property.config.ts' --exclude='vitest.setup.ts'
--exclude='tsconfig.json'             --exclude='tsconfig.test.json'
--exclude='esbuild.config.mjs'

Appended to the existing 14-exclude rsync block in scripts/build-plugins.sh — no second copy step, no manifest edit. The mirror's package.json already ships with devDependencies stripped, so the tree is now self-consistent: no file in it references a tool the manifest does not name.

The ratchet that keeps it dropped

tests/plugins/test-hooks-config-exclusion.sh has the same two halves as the #3971 mirror test, because a one-shot deletion can be undone by any future exclude-list edit:

halfasserts
A — shipped treenone of the seven exist under plugins/ork/hooks/, while bin/run-hook.mjs, hooks.json and package.json still do (deleting the tree cannot pass)
B — the real exclude list, exercisedthe excludes are extracted from build-plugins.sh and dry-run rsynced: the seven names are absent AND the payload files survive (removing an exclude cannot pass quietly)

Half B runs the repo's own rsync flags, so it exercises the real filter — and it parses output from both rsync dialects (macOS openrsync, CI GNU rsync) by matching plain filename lines only, never dialect-specific formats.

Verification

checkbeforeafter
ratchet test (targeted file)14 FAIL21 PASS, exit 0
configs under plugins/ork/hooks/70
shrink of the install—the seven files, ~14KB of dead text

Reproduce it

npm run build                       # regenerate the mirror with the new excludes
bash tests/plugins/test-hooks-config-exclusion.sh
git status --porcelain plugins/     # deletions only, generated by the build
The tests themselves were never shipped — the build dropped them long ago. What shipped was the equipment for tests that could not exist there. #4030 finishes the thought.
